content.thinking:
I'm figuring out the full file structure now, checking which imports and builder conventions from the project's API I'll need to set this up correctly.

Now I'm sketching the treasure hoard scene itself: a chest at the back with an open lid, a mound of gold coins built from a lathe shape, scattered coin cylinders, glowing gems, a crown, goblets, and extra flourishes like gold bars and a necklace, all composed through the builder's part and paint helpers with randomized placement for variety.

Working out the hinge geometry for the opened lid — I'm setting up the arch outline and rotating the extrude axes so the lid tilts back around the back hinge edge instead of just redrawing it flat.

Checking the perpendicularity confirms the rotation is consistent, and the outside-facing direction works out correctly when open. Now I'm defining the lid's arch outline as a set of coordinate points forming a rounded dome shape, which I'll need to smooth into a curve.

For the hinge thickness I'm setting a position offset, and treating the lid as a solid extrusion rather than worrying about a hollow interior. Inside the chest, I'm planning a gold coin mound using a lathe shape sitting atop a thin filled slab near the chest's opening, with the body box top and fill box positioned so the coins appear to rise slightly above the rim. I'm also sketching out iron strap bands wrapping around the body at several x-offsets.

Now I'm working out the coin scatter: generating a small cylinder geometry for each coin, then randomly distributing dozens of them across the mound surface using a height profile function, keeping the chest axis-aligned rather than rotated. Since there's a part-count limit, I'm planning to merge the coin instances into a few grouped geometries by color using a dummy object to bake transforms before merging, making sure all merged geometries share the same indexed format.

Separately, since the gem geometries are non-indexed polyhedrons, I'll keep those as individual parts rather than merging them with the coins. I'm also adding a few coin stacks as small rods with striped shading, and considering whether to add decal-style texture detail to the top coin faces.

For scattered coins on the floor, I'll use flat card-like planes with a coin SVG texture (emblem design), positioned mostly on the floor rather than the mound, aiming for around 25 flat coins plus the mirrored set. For gems, I'm setting up an array of colored octahedrons/icosahedrons (ruby, sapphire, emerald, amethyst, aqua) each with a glow effect at moderate strength, forming a crystal cluster.

Now I'm designing hexagonal-sided spikes for the crystal cluster using a spike helper with configurable sides, wrapped in glow, plus a crown piece on the mound built from a lathed outline with a thin ring profile and five spike points capped with small orb tips.

I'm also positioning the mound and chest in the scene -- defining the mound center and radius so it spills slightly into the chest's footprint, letting coins appear to overflow from an open chest against a mound behind it, while keeping overlapping geometry hidden inside the chest body.

Working out a height function for the mound by interpolating between a set of radius-height points to create a smooth bump shape, then placing coins at radii under the mound's edge so they sit naturally along that curved profile.

Defining the goblet outline points...

For variety, I'm planning to add a jewel band of small gem spheres around the bowl, and set up one goblet tipped on its side using a lathe with a tilted horizontal axis so the rim and foot both rest naturally on the floor.

Then I'm placing three goblets total: one standing gold-colored goblet, one silver-ish one with a red wine disc inside, and one lying tipped over, plus a mound of gold coins poking up from the bowl of one goblet with a gem on top for extra detail.

For the stem decoration, I'll add a small torus ring at the knop instead of painting a band. I'm also stacking gold bars in a pyramid arrangement nearby, and switching to a cel-shaded gold material with a brighter top face and darker base tone to give everything a saturated, stylized look.

I'm defining consistent cel-shaded materials for the other parts too: wood grain for the chest, cool-toned silver, dark bluish iron straps, and a red cel velvet material for a small tufted cushion placed under the crown.

Now I'm positioning the cushion and crown on the mound, computing their coordinates relative to the mound center so they sit correctly on the slope, then checking the overall scene footprint stays within a reasonable size. I'm also considering adding a glowing crystal cluster behind the right side and possibly a stone rubble plinth disc as a base for the whole composition.

For the base disc, I'll build it as a lathe profile with a slight cobbled edge, painted dark purple, roughly 1.45 radius. I decide to keep the vertical offset simple by letting other objects sink slightly into the disc rather than adding a precise Y offset, since the overlap is minor and won't be noticeable.

Estimating overall height: the chest body sits around 0.36 tall, the open lid extends up to about 0.95m, and crystals rise to roughly 0.6m, so the whole piece lands near 1m tall, which feels right. Now I'm detailing the chest itself—a wooden box body, metal corner bands, and a small gold lock plate on the front face.

Skipping extra decor for now, I'm working out the lid's open angle at 105 degrees, computing the rotated basis vectors and verifying the thickness direction stays consistent with the hinge positioned at the back top.

I'm figuring out where the lid's interior face points once rotated, then sketching a thin velvet-red lining rectangle positioned just above the lid's bottom wall to avoid z-fighting with it.

Shifting to the chest's contents: I'm building a flat coin fill as a shallow box sized to the chest's interior, plus a smaller lathed mound piece sitting on top to suggest a pile of coins spilling over the rim.

Working out a path for the chain from chest down to floor, verifying it clears the mound radius, and placing small white pearl spheres along it with a gem pendant at the end. I'll also scatter loose gems across the mound and floor for extra detail.

Adding gem helper logic...

For coin stacks, I'm building cylinder geometry with painted horizontal stripes for the rims, varying stack heights, and lighter gold disks on top. For the treasure sack, I'm sketching a lathe profile outline for a burlap sack shape with gold spilling out.

I'm checking the burlap sack shape for self-intersections, then working out where to place the rope tie, spilling coins, and the overall layout coordinates so the chest, mound, and sack don't overlap awkwardly in the scene.

I'm also figuring out placements for the crown on its cushion, the goblets standing and lying at various positions, and a crystal cluster behind the mound, making sure their bases sit logically against the mound's edge without clipping through it.

Working out the pearl chain path too, adjusting the end point to avoid colliding with the mound, and repositioning the bars so everything stays clear of overlapping geometry.

Now I'm placing the coin sack toward the front left with coins spilling toward positive x, and arranging the coin stacks and mound to check their distances stay outside each other's footprints. I'm also sizing the floor disc radius and center so it covers the chest, goblets, and crystals without clipping any of them.

Switching to scattering loose coins and cards across the floor within a ring around the mound, adjusting their vertical placement so they sit just above the disc surface instead of sinking into it, and considering merging the coin cylinders into a single geometry for efficiency.

I'm defining a generic coin-placement helper that takes position, tilt, and yaw and pushes transforms into color-indexed arrays, using three gold shades for the coins and keeping segment count low (8 sides) to control the triangle budget across roughly 170 coins.

I'm setting up a cell-based paint function for the coin mound: for each point it computes a cell distance pattern, uses a hashed id to pick between a few gold tones, darkens edges between cells, and shades the top faces differently from the sides based on surface normal.

Now I'm designing the crown geometry: a lathed band with five upright gold spikes topped by small orbs, plus glowing gems embedded around the band, and I'm adding a couple of arching sweeps across the top to give it a more ornate look.

I'm placing an orb atop the arches and sizing the arch/spike radii to fit together, spacing 8 spikes evenly at offset angles so they interleave with the arches rather than overlap. I'll also add a small jewelled ornament to the belt-lid for extra detail.

I'm skipping a lid-top gem and instead putting a glowing ruby on the chest lock plate, plus a gold crest emblem plane on the front of the chest between the side bands, sized and positioned to avoid the bands and lock plate.

Now I'm adding wood grain texture to the front panel with custom paint logic, working out seam line positions based on vertical plank spacing.

Writing wood shader code...

Settling on a 1024 paint size for safety, then setting up a seeded random generator and helper functions for placing parts with optional rotation, plus logic for merging coin geometries.

I'm defining a function to add a randomly-colored coin cylinder at a given position and orientation, applying a transform matrix to bake in the placement, then pushing it into the appropriate color bucket—planning to scatter around 150 of these across the mound.

For the mound coins, I'm randomizing angle and radius within a circular patch, computing height from a slope function, and applying a small random tilt so coins look naturally scattered rather than perfectly flat. For the sack, I'm placing a smaller cluster of spilled coins near the sack's mouth with slight position jitter and minor tilts to suggest they've tumbled out.

Now I'm setting up scattered floor coins arranged in a ring pattern around a center point, orienting each with its own flow direction so they look naturally strewn about, then defining the gem generator function that builds different polyhedral shapes (icosahedron, octahedron) with varied color and scale per gem type.

I'm placing twelve smaller gems across the mound while checking they don't overlap the crown area, then adding three larger accent gems at deliberately chosen mound positions using a helper function to compute their height on the terrain.

Now I'm setting up a crystal cluster near one edge of the mound, planning five spikes with varied directions, lengths, and radii that lean outward, using a spike-generation function that takes a base point, direction, length, radius, and color.

I'm picking crystal colors like magical cyan, violet, and pink, then building a goblet function using a lathed outline profile with a torus knop on the stem for upright versions, while considering how to adjust it for a goblet lying on its side.

For the lying goblet, I'm simplifying by just reorienting the lathe along a tilted axis so the bowl points outward, skipping extra gem details and adding a few spilled coins nearby for effect.

I'm working out the vertical placement so the bowl rim just touches the floor disc while the foot floats slightly above it, adding a small axis droop so the bowl end sits lower than the foot. For standing goblets I'll set them sinking slightly into the disc at y=0.04, and I'm using that same offset as the base reference for positioning the chest body and lid heights.

I'm restructuring the chest with a consistent floor reference, adding a dark iron skirt base beneath the main body, then stacking the body, hinge, and lid fill on top of that, with band widths and corner bracket positions calculated to align with the new body center.

Still placing details... adding rivets, the gold lock plate with keyhole cutout, and positioning the lid hinge at the back edge.

For the lid itself, I'm mirroring the arch band structure with offset hinges, placing cylindrical rod knuckles for the hinge joint, and defining a scaled arch outline function for the lid's curved shape.

Adding lid wood bevel and smoothing, marking bottom corners sharp while letting the arch points round out, then moving to the lining extrusion geometry.

Now I'm designing an emblem texture for the shield shape—a crest with gold trim, a diamond pattern, and a red inner gem, meant to sit as a small plane on the chest front.

I'm placing the shield decal at around y 0.24 with size 0.17x0.2, positioning it to clear the lock plate above and the surrounding body bands, checking the z-offset lines up just in front of the torso surface.

Now I'm skipping the chest side decals and moving to the gold bars: stacking them in rows (3, then 2, then 1) with slight z-spacing, then adding a small stamp decal on the top face of the topmost bar in each column, using a simple outlined rectangle-and-star design in darker gold.

I decide it's simplest to just put the stamp on every bar's top face raised slightly — hidden ones won't matter since they're covered by the bar above. I'm skipping yaw rotation on the bars to keep things simple, then moving on to shaping the sack with a lathe geometry and painting it with a mottled burlap texture.

For the rope, I'm adding a torus shape positioned at the sack's neck, colored dark brown. Then I'm figuring out placement for a decorative patch on the sack — considering a coin emblem decal on the front, calculating the correct z-position based on the sack's radius at that height so it sits flush against the curved surface.

Working through coin stack placement...

Adding a top coin cap with a decal face and some spilled coins near the stacks, then setting up sparkle card accents positioned above the gems and crown with star textures and upward-facing frames.

I'm adjusting the sparkle card anchor so it centers properly above each gem, then scattering small rock details along the disc's rim for texture and painting the disc edge with a cobblestone color pattern.

I'm skipping the torch and candle ideas, but adding a small red wine goblet with a defined bowl shape and a pile of tiny gold coin spheres nestled inside the chalice for extra detail.

Now I'm detailing the goblet's gems—placing a ring of small glowing spheres around the bowl in alternating colors, with a gold hemisphere topped by rubies, then setting up a reusable goblet function parameterized by position, material, gem color, and contents before writing out the actual part placement code.

Still writing styles...

Still building the mound geometry...

Now I'm working out the lid extrusion with its wood color and a trim band around the edge, setting positions and bevel thicknesses for each part.

I check that the hinge sits exactly at the back top edge of the body so the lid pivots correctly when opened at a wide angle, verifying the lid clears the body and swings backward properly. I also set the floor height constant and work out the crown and cushion placement on top, calculating the base height from the box geometry so the cushion and crown sit correctly stacked.

I'm sketching the crown's lathe profile for the band shape, adding gold trim rings via torus shapes at specific radii, and positioning eight spikes evenly around the crown using angular offsets.

Each spike gets a small gem orb at its tip, plus decorative gems embedded in the band and a larger central gem on the front, and I'm topping the crown off with arched sweeps and a final orb finial.
